title: hubble_gradient.ipynb

canonical_node.axiom: The chi-field modifies the effective gravitational constant as G_eff(z) = G / (1 + chi(z)), producing a smooth sigmoid transition in the Hubble constant from local (H=73.5) to CMB (H=67.4) values over redshift.
definitions: chi-field: a scalar field with value chi(z) at redshift z, derived from a Lagrangian structure.
G_eff(z): effective gravitational constant at redshift z, modified by the chi-field.
H(z): Hubble constant as a function of redshift, following a sigmoid profile.
H_CMB: Planck CMB value of the Hubble constant, 67.4 km/s/Mpc.
H_local: SH0ES local value of the Hubble constant, 73.5 km/s/Mpc.
z_transition: redshift at which the transition occurs, approximately 0.3.
5 match: statistical consistency at the five-sigma level, a standard for discovery claims in particle physics.
derivation: The chi-field modifies gravity via G_eff(z) = G / (1 + chi(z)).
At high redshift, chi -> 0, so G_eff -> G, recovering standard gravity and Planck H.
At low redshift, chi is nonzero, suppressing G_eff and increasing the measured H.
The resulting H(z) follows a sigmoid: H(z) = H_CMB + (H_local  H_CMB) / (1 + exp(k(z  z_transition))).
The chi-field parameters are set by the Lagrangian, not fitted to the Hubble data.
The notebook computes the chi-field H(z) curve and compares it to observational data, claiming a 5 match.
canonical_node.action: The system should compute the chi-field prediction for H(z) and compare it to observational data, specifically the SH0ES and Planck measurements, to test the Hubble tension resolution.
boundary: This document does not provide a full derivation of the chi-field Lagrangian or the modified Friedmann equations.
It does not include the actual code or data analysis steps of the notebook.
It does not claim to resolve the Hubble tension definitively; it claims a 5 match and a future test with Euclid.
It does not address other cosmological tensions or anomalies beyond the Hubble tension and DESI DR2 compatibility.
test: Compute the chi-field H(z) curve using the stated formula and compare to observational data at multiple redshifts.
Verify the claimed 5 statistical match using appropriate statistical methods.
Check the compatibility with DESI DR2 evidence for dark energy evolution.
Await the Euclid spacecraft data in October 2026 to test the sigmoid prediction against alternatives.
